user=github-changelog-generator
project=github-changelog-generator

# Version Range
# Specify the starting tag for changelog generation
since-tag=1.0.0
# Optionally specify an ending tag
# due-tag=2.0.0

# Unreleased Changes
# Include unreleased changes (commits since last tag)
unreleased=true
unreleased-label=**Unreleased**

output=CHANGELOG.md
header=# Changelog

# Use ISO 8601 date format
date-format=%Y-%m-%d

compare-link=true

enhancement-labels=enhancement,feature,Feature,Enhancement
enhancement-label=**New Features:**

bug-label=**Fixed Bugs:**

# Advanced Configuration Example

This directory contains a comprehensive example of configuring the GitHub Changelog Generator with advanced options for customizing changelog output.

## Contents

- `.github_changelog_generator` - Complete configuration file with detailed comments
- `CHANGELOG.md` - Sample output demonstrating the configuration in action
- `README.md` - This documentation file

## Configuration Overview

The `.github_changelog_generator` file demonstrates the full range of configuration options available for customizing your changelog generation.

### Repository Settings

```
user=github-changelog-generator
project=github-changelog-generator
```

Specifies the GitHub repository owner and project name.

### Version Range Configuration

```
since-tag=1.0.0
due-tag=2.0.0
```

- `since-tag`: Starting point for changelog generation (inclusive)
- `due-tag`: Ending point for changelog generation (optional)

### Unreleased Changes

```
unreleased=true
unreleased-label=**Unreleased**
```

Include commits and PRs since the last tag in an "Unreleased" section at the top of the changelog.

### Output Configuration

```
output=CHANGELOG.md
header=# Changelog
date-format=%Y-%m-%d
compare-link=true
```

- `output`: Output filename
- `header`: Custom header text (can be multi-line)
- `date-format`: Date formatting using strftime syntax
- `compare-link`: Include GitHub comparison links between versions

### Label-Based Sections

The configuration groups issues and pull requests into sections based on their GitHub labels:

#### New Features
```
enhancement-labels=enhancement,feature,Feature,Enhancement
enhancement-label=**New Features:**
```

#### Bug Fixes
```
bug-labels=bug,fix,bugfix,Bug,Fix
bug-label=**Fixed Bugs:**
```

#### Breaking Changes
```
breaking-labels=breaking-change,breaking,Breaking Change
breaking-label=**Breaking Changes:**
breaking-prefix=⚠ BREAKING CHANGE:
```

The `breaking-prefix` adds a visual indicator to breaking changes.

#### Security Updates
```
security-labels=security,Security
security-label=**Security:**
```

#### Documentation
```
documentation-labels=documentation,docs,Documentation
documentation-label=**Documentation:**
```

#### Deprecated Features
```
deprecated-labels=deprecated,Deprecated
deprecated-label=**Deprecated:**
```

#### Removed Features
```
removed-labels=removed,Removed
removed-label=**Removed:**
```

### Filtering Options

#### Exclude Labels
```
exclude-labels=duplicate,question,invalid,wontfix,wont-fix,skip-changelog,no-changelog
```

Issues and PRs with these labels will not appear in the changelog.

#### Include Labels
```
include-labels=changelog
```

When uncommented, only issues/PRs with these labels will be included (whitelist mode).

#### Exclude Tags
```
exclude-tags-regex=^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+-(alpha|beta|rc)
```

Excludes pre-release tags from the changelog using regex patterns.

### Pull Request Configuration

```
add-pr-wo-labels=true
merge-prefix=**Merged pull requests:**
```

- `add-pr-wo-labels`: Include PRs that don't have any recognized labels
- `merge-prefix`: Section header for unlabeled merged PRs

### Issue Configuration

```
add-issues-wo-labels=false
issue-line-labels=ALL
```

- `add-issues-wo-labels`: Whether to include issues without labels
- `issue-line-labels`: Show labels inline with issues (ALL or specific labels)

### Formatting Options

```
simple-list=false
usernames-as-github-logins=true
```

- `simple-list`: Use simple list format vs. full format with details
- `usernames-as-github-logins`: Display GitHub usernames as @username

### Performance Options

```
http-cache=true
max-issues=0
```

- `http-cache`: Enable HTTP caching to speed up repeated runs
- `max-issues`: Limit number of issues to fetch (0 = unlimited)

## Usage

### Using the Configuration File

Generate a changelog using this configuration:

```bash
github_changelog_generator --config examples/advanced_config/.github_changelog_generator
```

### Overriding Configuration Options

You can override any configuration option from the command line:

```bash
github_changelog_generator \
  --config examples/advanced_config/.github_changelog_generator \
  --since-tag v1.5.0 \
  --unreleased false
```

### Validating Configuration

To validate the configuration without generating a changelog:

```bash
github_changelog_generator \
  --config examples/advanced_config/.github_changelog_generator \
  --help
```

If the configuration file is valid, the help text will display normally.

## Customization Tips

### Custom Sections

You can create custom sections by defining new label groups:

```
custom-labels=custom,special
custom-label=**Custom Section:**
```

### Multi-line Headers

The header option supports multi-line text for rich changelog introductions:

```
header=# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

See [Conventional Commits](https://conventionalcommits.org) for commit guidelines.
```

### Date Formats

Common date format strings:
- ISO 8601: `%Y-%m-%d` (2026-07-28)
- US Format: `%m/%d/%Y` (07/28/2026)
- Full: `%B %d, %Y` (July 28, 2026)
- Short: `%b %d, %Y` (Jul 28, 2026)

### Base File Integration

To prepend an existing changelog:

```
base=HISTORY.md
```

The tool will merge new entries with the existing content.

## Best Practices

1. **Label Consistency**: Establish consistent labeling conventions in your repository
2. **Breaking Changes**: Always use dedicated labels for breaking changes to highlight them
3. **Exclude Appropriately**: Exclude housekeeping labels (duplicate, wontfix) to keep the changelog clean
4. **Version Range**: Use `since-tag` to generate incremental changelogs
5. **Cache Usage**: Enable `http-cache` for faster repeated runs during testing
6. **Security Section**: Use dedicated security labels for vulnerability fixes
7. **Regular Updates**: Generate changelog updates with each release

## Example Workflow

1. Configure your `.github_changelog_generator` file in your repository root
2. Label your issues and PRs appropriately
3. Generate changelog before each release:
   ```bash
   github_changelog_generator --future-release v2.0.0
   ```
4. Review and commit the updated CHANGELOG.md
5. Create your release with the changelog content

## See Also

- [Main Documentation](../../README.md)
- [GitHub Changelog Generator Wiki](https://github.com/github-changelog-generator/github-changelog-generator/wiki)
- [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/)
- [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/)

# This demonstrates advanced configuration options for customizing changelog generation

# Repository Configuration
user=github-changelog-generator
project=github-changelog-generator

# Version Range
# Specify the starting tag for changelog generation
since-tag=1.0.0
# Optionally specify an ending tag
# due-tag=2.0.0

# Unreleased Changes
# Include unreleased changes (commits since last tag)
unreleased=true
unreleased-label=**Unreleased**

# Base File
# Prepend existing changelog file (optional)
# base=HISTORY.md

# Output Configuration
output=CHANGELOG.md
header=# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

# Date Format
# Use ISO 8601 date format
date-format=%Y-%m-%d

# Compare Links
# Include comparison links between versions
compare-link=true

# Label Configuration
# Enhancement/Feature Labels
enhancement-labels=enhancement,feature,Feature,Enhancement
enhancement-label=**New Features:**

# Bug Fix Labels
bug-labels=bug,fix,bugfix,Bug,Fix
bug-label=**Fixed Bugs:**

# Breaking Change Labels
breaking-labels=breaking-change,breaking,Breaking Change
breaking-label=**Breaking Changes:**
breaking-prefix=⚠ BREAKING CHANGE:

# Deprecated Features
deprecated-labels=deprecated,Deprecated
deprecated-label=**Deprecated:**

# Removed Features
removed-labels=removed,Removed
removed-label=**Removed:**

# Security Updates
security-labels=security,Security
security-label=**Security:**

# Documentation Updates
documentation-labels=documentation,docs,Documentation
documentation-label=**Documentation:**

# Exclude Labels
# Issues/PRs with these labels won't appear in changelog
exclude-labels=duplicate,question,invalid,wontfix,wont-fix,skip-changelog,no-changelog

# Issue/PR Filtering
# Only include issues with specific labels (optional)
# include-labels=changelog

# Additional Options
# Add author of each change
add-pr-wo-labels=true
# Include issues without labels
add-issues-wo-labels=false

# Pull Request Configuration
merge-prefix=**Merged pull requests:**
# Filter pull requests by base branch
# pr-label=**Merged PRs:**

# Issue Configuration
issue-line-labels=ALL
# Configure issue prefix
# configure-sections={"enhancement":{"prefix":"**New Features:**","labels":["enhancement","feature"]}}

# Formatting
# Simple list format (alternative: full)
simple-list=false

# Author/Contributor Options
# Show author username for each entry
usernames-as-github-logins=true

# Exclude specific tags from changelog
exclude-tags-regex=^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+-(alpha|beta|rc)

# HTTP Cache
# Enable HTTP cache to speed up repeated runs
http-cache=true

# Max Issues
# Limit the number of issues to fetch (0 = unlimited)
max-issues=0

# Verbose Output
# verbose=true

# Advanced Configuration Example

This directory contains a comprehensive example of configuring the GitHub Changelog Generator with advanced options for customizing changelog output.

## Contents

- `.github_changelog_generator` - Complete configuration file with detailed comments
- `CHANGELOG.md` - Sample output demonstrating the configuration in action
- `README.md` - This documentation file

## Configuration Overview

The `.github_changelog_generator` file demonstrates the full range of configuration options available for customizing your changelog generation.

### Repository Settings

```
user=github-changelog-generator
project=github-changelog-generator
```

Specifies the GitHub repository owner and project name.

### Version Range Configuration

```
since-tag=1.0.0
due-tag=2.0.0
```

- `since-tag`: Starting point for changelog generation (inclusive)
- `due-tag`: Ending point for changelog generation (optional)

### Unreleased Changes

```
unreleased=true
unreleased-label=**Unreleased**
```

Include commits and PRs since the last tag in an "Unreleased" section at the top of the changelog.

### Output Configuration

```
output=CHANGELOG.md
header=# Changelog
date-format=%Y-%m-%d
compare-link=true
```

- `output`: Output filename
- `header`: Custom header text (can be multi-line)
- `date-format`: Date formatting using strftime syntax
- `compare-link`: Include GitHub comparison links between versions

### Label-Based Sections

The configuration groups issues and pull requests into sections based on their GitHub labels:

#### New Features
```
enhancement-labels=enhancement,feature,Feature,Enhancement
enhancement-label=**New Features:**
```

#### Bug Fixes
```
bug-labels=bug,fix,bugfix,Bug,Fix
bug-label=**Fixed Bugs:**
```

#### Breaking Changes
```
breaking-labels=breaking-change,breaking,Breaking Change
breaking-label=**Breaking Changes:**
breaking-prefix=⚠ BREAKING CHANGE:
```

The `breaking-prefix` adds a visual indicator to breaking changes.

#### Security Updates
```
security-labels=security,Security
security-label=**Security:**
```

#### Documentation
```
documentation-labels=documentation,docs,Documentation
documentation-label=**Documentation:**
```

#### Deprecated Features
```
deprecated-labels=deprecated,Deprecated
deprecated-label=**Deprecated:**
```

#### Removed Features
```
removed-labels=removed,Removed
removed-label=**Removed:**
```

### Filtering Options

#### Exclude Labels
```
exclude-labels=duplicate,question,invalid,wontfix,wont-fix,skip-changelog,no-changelog
```

Issues and PRs with these labels will not appear in the changelog.

#### Include Labels
```
include-labels=changelog
```

When uncommented, only issues/PRs with these labels will be included (whitelist mode).

#### Exclude Tags
```
exclude-tags-regex=^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+-(alpha|beta|rc)
```

Excludes pre-release tags from the changelog using regex patterns.

### Pull Request Configuration

```
add-pr-wo-labels=true
merge-prefix=**Merged pull requests:**
```

- `add-pr-wo-labels`: Include PRs that don't have any recognized labels
- `merge-prefix`: Section header for unlabeled merged PRs

### Issue Configuration

```
add-issues-wo-labels=false
issue-line-labels=ALL
```

- `add-issues-wo-labels`: Whether to include issues without labels
- `issue-line-labels`: Show labels inline with issues (ALL or specific labels)

### Formatting Options

```
simple-list=false
usernames-as-github-logins=true
```

- `simple-list`: Use simple list format vs. full format with details
- `usernames-as-github-logins`: Display GitHub usernames as @username

### Performance Options

```
http-cache=true
max-issues=0
```

- `http-cache`: Enable HTTP caching to speed up repeated runs
- `max-issues`: Limit number of issues to fetch (0 = unlimited)

## Usage

### Using the Configuration File

Generate a changelog using this configuration:

```bash
github_changelog_generator --config examples/advanced_config/.github_changelog_generator
```

### Overriding Configuration Options

You can override any configuration option from the command line:

```bash
github_changelog_generator \
  --config examples/advanced_config/.github_changelog_generator \
  --since-tag v1.5.0 \
  --unreleased false
```

### Validating Configuration

To validate the configuration without generating a changelog:

```bash
github_changelog_generator \
  --config examples/advanced_config/.github_changelog_generator \
  --help
```

If the configuration file is valid, the help text will display normally.

## Customization Tips

### Custom Sections

You can create custom sections by defining new label groups:

```
custom-labels=custom,special
custom-label=**Custom Section:**
```

### Multi-line Headers

The header option supports multi-line text for rich changelog introductions:

```
header=# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

See [Conventional Commits](https://conventionalcommits.org) for commit guidelines.
```

### Date Formats

Common date format strings:
- ISO 8601: `%Y-%m-%d` (2026-07-28)
- US Format: `%m/%d/%Y` (07/28/2026)
- Full: `%B %d, %Y` (July 28, 2026)
- Short: `%b %d, %Y` (Jul 28, 2026)

### Base File Integration

To prepend an existing changelog:

```
base=HISTORY.md
```

The tool will merge new entries with the existing content.

## Best Practices

1. **Label Consistency**: Establish consistent labeling conventions in your repository
2. **Breaking Changes**: Always use dedicated labels for breaking changes to highlight them
3. **Exclude Appropriately**: Exclude housekeeping labels (duplicate, wontfix) to keep the changelog clean
4. **Version Range**: Use `since-tag` to generate incremental changelogs
5. **Cache Usage**: Enable `http-cache` for faster repeated runs during testing
6. **Security Section**: Use dedicated security labels for vulnerability fixes
7. **Regular Updates**: Generate changelog updates with each release

## Example Workflow

1. Configure your `.github_changelog_generator` file in your repository root
2. Label your issues and PRs appropriately
3. Generate changelog before each release:
   ```bash
   github_changelog_generator --future-release v2.0.0
   ```
4. Review and commit the updated CHANGELOG.md
5. Create your release with the changelog content

## See Also

- [Main Documentation](../../README.md)
- [GitHub Changelog Generator Wiki](https://github.com/github-changelog-generator/github-changelog-generator/wiki)
- [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/)
- [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/)
